name: Cross-conversation recall store
description: Finds the earlier conversation an unclear message refers to by relevance across the whole history, not only the most recent threads.
purpose: Help a person pick up a thread from their own earlier conversations without restating what they already said.
approach: Rank a person's earlier conversations of the same user or team by relevance to the current message and load only the best few.
out_of_scope: Searching documents, notes or cards for background material.
milestones: 1. The conversation a person means is among the first three results for every labelled case, and no other user's conversation appears in any result.
knowledge: Recall must be relevance-first over the whole history, with recency only a small boost and a small floor of the newest conversations, because time cutoffs lost old but relevant threads. Scanning every file in full does not scale, so a cheap per-file digest shortlists candidates and only a capped few are fully loaded. Paraphrased questions that share no words with a past thread remain a known gap for term-based ranking.
measures_of_success: The conversation a person means is returned among the first few results, including old ones and paraphrases, no conversation from another user or outside the requested scope ever appears, and call cost stays flat as history grows.
parameters: Per call: the query text, a scope (user, team, since, participant), an optional conversation id to exclude, the maximum number of conversations, a character budget, and optional opaque filters such as a time range. Construction takes a corpus root and a sessions directory.
inputs: A natural-language query or the latest user message, a scope dictionary, and for the current-conversation call a conversation id and the number of recent turns considered.
outputs: A conversation context holding rendered text slices from the selected conversations, plus a degraded note when a hard filter matched nothing and the store fell back to relevance only.
effects: None beyond outputs apart from in-memory caches of per-file digests and parsed conversations; it never writes conversations and never raises, returning an empty context on failure.
usage_notes: Call before planning so that follow-up messages become self-contained goals. Always pass the scope of the asking user so isolation is enforced; add a backend by implementing the same protocol rather than changing callers.

name: Feedback-to-guidance loop
description: Keeps a person's corrections as standing guidance, apart from one-off requests, and shows each one on the turns where it applies.
purpose: Help the assistant stop repeating a mistake a person has already corrected, so they only have to say it once.
approach: Turn each correction into guidance kept apart from one-off requests and shown where it bears on the turn.
out_of_scope: One-off requests, which are not promoted to permanent rules.
milestones: 1. After a standing correction is stored, the next relevant turn shows it, and no correction that does not bear on the turn is shown, across the feedback sequences.
knowledge: Remembering everything gives perfect recall but turns one-time requests into permanent rules and crowds every prompt, so a ledger separating standing from one-off corrections is needed. The current weakness is precision: with no relevance cut below the card limit, an unrelated rule is shown while room remains. Guidance enters the system prompt as behaviour to follow, not optional context.
measures_of_success: After a standing correction is stored, the next relevant turn shows it, corrections that do not bear on the turn are not shown, and one-off requests are not promoted.
parameters: Cards directory, optional dynamic guidance loader, vector store, provider and model for relevance filtering, a card manager factory, and the number of cards selected per turn.
inputs: A user message and caller scope metadata for selection; correction text, author, location and run dispositions for the ledger.
outputs: A list of guidance cards with bodies for the applicable-guidance block; a catalog and single card reads on demand.
effects: The ledger records observations and writes guidance cards on standing corrections; selection itself is read-only; never raises.
usage_notes: Wire the provider into the orchestrator so selection runs once before planning; rank by relevance when the card limit has room, add a vector or model filter where precision matters.

name: Verbatim feedback ledger
description: Keeps what a person asked for and tracks what became of it, so a standing rule keeps applying after its first use and a one-time request never turns into a rule.
purpose: Keep each correction a person gives in their own words, with author and time, and track how far it has been followed.
approach: Store each correction verbatim with its author and time, and record its status from the run's own structured report.
out_of_scope: Paraphrasing or summarising a correction, and grading one.
milestones: 1. Feedback cases passed by the ledger guidance arm: 16 of 16, with each standing rule carried into a guidance card.
knowledge: Replying is not doing: a timestamp after a note closes it whether or not it was honoured, so status comes from the run's own structured disposition, and an unrecognised disposition leaves the item untouched. A person's status always outranks a run's. A standing rule is never finished by one application, so it stays in force and carries how far it has got; it is also written to a guidance card so retrieval carries it forward.
measures_of_success: A correction appears in the ledger as given, a standing rule becomes a guidance card shown on later turns, and a one-time request or the uncarded half of a mixed note never reaches guidance. Standing conditions: Keep every correction stored verbatim with author and time. Keep corrections across restarts. Keep one-time requests separate from standing rules.
parameters: The ledger takes an optional file path, a read-only flag, a flag requiring human acceptance before a run's done counts, and an optional pluggable store. Items carry card, source, item id, author, text, kind (request or standing), state and history.
inputs: Observed items (the person's words, author, time, source) and a run's account of what it did with each, opened by a disposition from a fixed vocabulary.
outputs: Ledger items with status lines, the open and standing sets, and guidance written for standing rules.
effects: Persists the whole document atomically and may write a guidance card per standing rule. A store that cannot be reached degrades to nothing recorded on read and a logged, swallowed failure on write.
usage_notes: Observe items when they arrive, record the run's account after each run, and let the guidance bridge carry standing rules. Supply a database-backed store when the host's durable record is not a file.

name: Scoped recent-context warm start
description: Keeps each work item's recent cards available to the next turn at no model cost, fenced so one work item's records never reach another.
purpose: Hands the next turn of a conversation the cards its last turns already found, so a short follow-up needs no restating.
approach: Stores each turn's selected cards under the work item's key and returns the relevant ones at the start of the next turn.
out_of_scope: Finding cards by meaning, and a follow-up that shares no words with the earlier turns it refers to.
milestones: 1. Every synthetic multi-turn follow-up case returns the right earlier cards, and no stale or cross-work-item card is returned.
knowledge: Cards are re-selected from scratch each turn under a short budget, so a follow-up paid full cost and a timeout left a turn with nothing. Scope tags fence one work item's records from another's, while untagged legacy records stay visible. A purely lexical gate misses a paraphrase that shares no word, which is a known limit.
measures_of_success: On synthetic multi-turn cases the right earlier cards come back for a follow-up, and no stale or cross-work-item card is ever returned. Standing conditions: Keep stale and cross-work-item cards from being returned. Spend no model call.
parameters: The file store takes a root directory and caps for turns, cards, preview length, record age and items per card, with separate larger caps for the global scope. Scope keys name a conversation, a work item or the global scope.
inputs: For record: scope keys, the selected cards and the user's text. For load: scope keys, then the current turn's text for filtering.
outputs: Recent card records merged across scopes, narrower scope winning, deduplicated by card id, then filtered by relevance, with optional item-usage hints and rendered blocks.
effects: Writes small per-scope files atomically. Both calls are best effort and never raise.
usage_notes: Record after each turn that selected cards and load at the start of the next. Always pass the work item's key so the fence applies, and treat the result as a warm fallback beside, not instead of, normal retrieval.

name: Scoped prediction store
description: Keeps each scope's learned patterns, live predictions and outcome log across turns and restarts, through a store that never raises into a turn, so a failed write costs that write and never a reply.
purpose: Remembers, for each scope, what an anticipation engine has learned, across turns and restarts.
approach: Saves each scope's patterns, predictions and outcome log, and returns them only to the scope they belong to.
out_of_scope: Judging whether a prediction was right, and sharing learned patterns across scopes.
milestones: 1. A store passes every persistence contract scenario (round trip, isolation, replace, expiry, view, clear, log, restart and tolerance) with no store call raising: all 12 cases pass on the file store. [met: 2026-10-22]
knowledge: The store sits behind a port so a consumer with its own database can supply one. Storage must be best-effort and never raise into a turn. Prediction quality is a separate unmeasured question: the engine logs each prediction against the actual next message, but no replayed corpus scores it.
measures_of_success: A store passes every contract scenario: round trip, isolation, replace, expiry, view, clear, log, restart and tolerance.
parameters: A scope key per call, patterns, predictions with an expiry time and optional views, and a log record.
inputs: Pattern and prediction records and the scope key.
outputs: The saved patterns, the unexpired predictions, a precomputed view text by prediction id, or nothing for a write.
effects: Writes persistent state (a file per scope and an outcome log in the file store) and drops expired predictions on load.
usage_notes: Implement the port's methods to add a backend and run the same contract scenarios against it; choose the file store for a lane, an in-memory store only as a reference.

name: Representative selection: which AI representative handles a request, and whose higher mind grounds it
description: Chooses, for every chat message, queued task and autopilot pass, the one AI representative that should handle it, from the quest's assigned representatives and their roles, the person's own ask and the thread it came from, so the work speaks with one voice and is grounded in the right representative's view.
purpose: Puts each request in the hands of the AI representative that fits it, consistently across chat, tasks and background work.
approach: Chooses the representative from structured assignment first, then from fit between the request and each assigned representative's role and quests, keeps a thread's representative for the work it spawns, and asks the person only when two fit equally.
out_of_scope: Writing a representative's persona or role, assigning representatives to quests, and what the chosen representative then does.
milestones: 1. A labelled set of requests exists (quests with several assigned representatives and roles, a named representative, a bare mention of a name, a task spawned from a chat, an equal fit), and persona_resolver_precedence has a recorded result on it. 2. thread_holds_its_rep keeps every spawned task on its thread's representative, and the selected arm matches the labels at least as often as today's, asking the person only on equal fits.
knowledge: Unconfirmed: proposed 2026-10-28 for the specification owner to confirm. The specification owner's direction (2026-10-28): a quest can have more than one AI representative, and representative selection is a key aspect of the library. Read in code on 2026-10-28: the library's persona resolver decides a queued task's persona by structured assignment, then an explicit ask judged by a model, then domain cards, then a structural fallback (runner/personas.py), and is listed today as part of run-queued-tasks, whose metric checks only that the configured persona runs; the host picks among a quest's assigned representatives with one fast-model call for chat and falls back to the person's default; the autopilot roster names representatives per quest with days and their own instructions. Nothing measures whether the choice was right, and nothing keeps a thread's representative for the tasks it spawns.
measures_of_success: The chosen representative matches the labelled fit; a task spawned from a chat keeps that chat's representative; a bare mention never selects; the person is asked only on an equal fit. Standing conditions: Never select a representative the person cannot see. Never decide from keywords in a model's own output.
parameters: The precedence of signals, whether a model judges fit and on which tier, the tie threshold that asks the person, and whether spawned work inherits the thread's representative.
inputs: The request, its thread and quest, the quest's assigned representatives with their roles and visibility, the autopilot roster, and any representative the person named.
outputs: The chosen representative (or none for the plain assistant), the reason, and whether the person was asked.
effects: At most one small model call per choice; the choice is recorded on the thread or task.
usage_notes: Selected today: persona_resolver_precedence for queued tasks; the host's chat classifier is host_assigned_classifier.

name: Guidance toward the long-term goal
description: Decides when and how a reply points the person at their quest's next milestone and its current metric reading, at the intent level that fits the moment (the goal in focus, the quest, or a representative's portfolio), and when it stays silent.
purpose: Keeps the person moving toward the end they are working for, without hijacking a simple question or nagging.
approach: The reply voice answers first. A directive about the long-term goal is added to it, saying when to add one short pointer, at which level, with the real milestone and reading, and when to leave it out; a grader checks both sides on labelled cases.
out_of_scope: Choosing the milestone or the metric (the quest and its intent hold them), creating or linking intents (only a person does), and the representative's standing view (hold-the-intents).
milestones: 1. The two-sided metric has a case set and a recorded result for the floor, the current reply voice and the guided arm. 2. The guided arm beats the current reply voice on the two-sided value, with no invented figure and no more awkward restraint cases.
knowledge: Unconfirmed: proposed 2026-10-29 from the 2026-10-27 accountability meeting transcript (spiritual_data_funding/human_context/meetings/transcripts/2026-10-27-accountability-meeting-1JByS08XMyrA7HJk5rVpRQaRJqG29wMyzUk9QfHMba8k.txt, 49:15 to 50:27) and the 2026-10-28 excerpt (hierarchy of intents, 24:44 to 25:50), for the specification owner to confirm. The direction: the assistant should generally encourage the person to move forward on the long-term goal, thinking in ESOI terms, aware of the next target milestone and the current metric, at whatever intent level makes sense for the context, and the metric must also catch awkward use of it.
measures_of_success: Nudge cases right and restraint cases right rise together, per intent level. Standing conditions: Never invent a milestone, date or figure. Answer the request first. Add no model call before the reply.
parameters: The directive text, the word limit of the reply and the model tier.
inputs: The quest, its next milestone and metric reading, the intent hierarchy it sits under (or, for a representative, its assigned quests), the conversation so far, and the message.
outputs: The reply, with or without one short pointer.
effects: None beyond the reply text; no added call.
usage_notes: Selected: guided_v2 (the LONG_TERM_GUIDANCE section of REPLY_VOICE_SYSTEM). reply_voice is the reply voice before it, guided the first candidate directive, no_nudge the floor.
